body:
scripts/auto-close-awaiting-verification.sh clears the `awaiting-verification`
label when ANY non-`new-usemame` comment appears after the label was applied,
on the reasoning that the reporter has engaged and their reply is the
verification signal.

The commenter is never checked against the reporter.

OBSERVED 2026-08-09 on #1372, filed by @bjekel: the sweep logged
"LABEL CLEARED — 1 reporter comment(s) since label applied" and removed it. The
comment was @stripeymonkey's, a third party, and it was not about @bjekel's bug
at all — they were asking where the cover-and-metadata enforcement button had
gone. @bjekel has still never said whether the v4.1.30 kepub series fix worked.

The consequence is not cosmetic. Clearing the label takes the issue off the
14-day auto-close path, so it now sits open forever with no verification from
anyone: too engaged to time out, not actually verified. The follow-up board also
reported it only as "needs triage", so the real state — nobody has confirmed the
fix — was invisible.

Fix shape: compare the commenter against the issue author. A reply from the
reporter clears the label as it does today. A comment from anyone else should
leave the label alone (at most note it), because a stranger's unrelated question
is not the reporter confirming their bug is gone.
title: awaiting-verification sweep counts a third party's comment as the reporter verifying
